Subject: Post-discovery: structured-output & tooling shortlist + next steps

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed plan so we can move to a short hands-on eval next week. I tried to keep this tight so your engineers can scan quickly.

What we heard
- Use case: ingestion + normalization of intake forms (medical referrals) into a structured EHR-friendly JSON. High accuracy on discrete fields (patient name, DOB, ICD codes) is critical; free-text notes can tolerate higher variance.
- Volume: expected 500–1,000 requests/day initially, spikes up to ~5k/day during campaign windows.
- Latency targets: P95 < 450ms preferred; willing to accept higher P95 for occasional large documents if we compensate with batching.
- Security: data stays in VPC/private deployment; SOC2 evidence required for procurement.

Redwood shortlists & rationale (for the eval)
- Candidate A: falcon-40b-instruct (quantized int8) — best token-cost balance for structured extraction when paired with KV prefix caching.
- Candidate B: llama-2-70b-chat (FP16) — stronger at edge-case name/alias resolution and complex context windows; higher infra cost.
- Candidate C: redwood-mini-13b (4-bit quant) — good for low-cost sampling and as a fallback tier for high-throughput bursts.

Evaluation focus (what we will measure)
1) Schema compliance: JSON outputs validated against your target schema (attached). Acceptance: >98% top-level keys present and proper types for critical fields.
2) Entity accuracy: micro-F1 on name/DOB/ICD extraction using the prompt_set we captured (attached sample).
3) Tool-calling behavior: tool (function) call correctness, idempotency on retries, and clear error / fallback semantics.
4) Latency and cost: P95 and per-1000-token cost estimate.

Attachments included
- acme_prompt_sets.csv (sample prompts & edge cases)
- structured_output_eval_plan.xlsx (detailed criteria + timeline)
- llm_benchmarks_july2026.pdf (our internal latency/cost baselines)

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
- Jordan: deliver the eval plan + ephemeral creds for a 48-hour private sandbox by Thu 08/06.
- Acme (Samira): share 200 deidentified sample records and confirm schema version (v2) by Thu 08/06.
- Rishi: scope SOC2 artifacts and a short checklist for procurement (ETA Fri 08/07).

If that looks right, I'll provision a small private endpoint and drop the sandbox link + HubSpot deal update.

Thanks —

Jordan Blake

Samira / Tom —

Great questions. Quick answers and pointers below; more detail is in the attached eval plan and the benchmark doc.

Latency (P95) guidance
- falcon-40b-instruct (quantized int8) on our Dedicated pool: typical P95 ~320–420ms for 512-token windows with continuous batching and KV caching.
- llama-2-70b-chat (FP16) on Dedicated: typical P95 ~480–700ms for similarly sized windows; better tail-case extraction but costs ~1.6–2x.
- Notes: benchmarks in llm_benchmarks_july2026.pdf table 2 show variance by sequence length; we will include your sample size in the sandbox to produce a site-specific run.

Retries & deduplication for tool-calls
- Redwood Tooling default: 3 retries with exponential backoff (200ms, 600ms, 1800ms) for transient 5xx/connection failures.
- Deduplication: each logical request is assigned a request_id and we apply an idempotency window (60s by default) to prevent duplicate external webhook invocations. You can adjust both settings at the route level.
- Failure semantics: on repeated webhook failure, the runtime can either: (a) return a structured error that the app can surface, or (b) route to a fallback model/fallback webhook if configured. We'll model both during the eval.

Schema validation visibility
- Our validator runs post-generation and emits a JSON path + failure code (type_mismatch, missing_key, extra_key, array_length_mismatch). See column "FailReason" in the attached eval spreadsheet.
- We can produce a per-record report that includes the raw output, the validation diff, and a suggested repair (e.g., cast to string, trim).

Proposed technical exercise (2 phases)
Phase 1 (3 days): smoke run — 200 deidentified samples you provide. Objective: measure schema pass rate, entity micro-F1, and P95. Deliverable: per-record validation report + summary dashboard.
Phase 2 (5–7 days): targeted A/B between falcon-40b-instruct (primary) and llama-2-70b-chat (control) on the 2k expanded sample set. Acceptance rule: pick model with >=0.5% higher F1 on critical fields with <=30% cost delta, and schema pass rate >97%.

Next actions I will take today
- Provision a private sandbox (48h) and upload ephemeral credentials to the HubSpot deal; I’ll paste the link once ready.
- Share the structured_output_eval_plan.xlsx and a short runbook for validators (attached).

If that plan works, can we lock Thu 08/06 for the sample delivery and kick off Phase 1 on Fri 08/07?

Best,
Jordan
